newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER NOT "IN-AND-OUT SITUATION"- NEW OWNER.
newsitem.headline: AMER NOT "IN-AND-OUT SITUATION"- NEW OWNER.

text.p: Purchasing a majority of Amer is not an in-and-out situation but an investment for years ahead, buyer Jonathan Bryan Guinness said on Monday.

In an interview with Reuters after announcing a preliminary agreement which still needs approval by the Finnish institutions which now control Amer, Guinness said he hoped for a benficial share price development to enable financing growth with shares.
"This is not an in-and-out situation," Guiness said.
"Amer could even be at the centre of a very powerful group," Guiness said, adding Wilson was Amer's most important asset.

Amer said earlier its four main owners who now control 90.5 percent of votes still have to approve the planned sale of 1.1 million vote-strong K-shares to Guiness in the restructuring, which would eventually give Guiness 58.4 percent of votes. The price of the deal was 301 million markka.

Guiness said his investment horizon for Amer was "certainly years" and that he could help the group's current turnaround with knowledge he acquired while on the board of Irish Guinness, which he left in 1988.

After leaving Guinness when his family's holding shrank too low to justify two members on the board -- today it has none -- Guinness has considered himself mostly a writer, and authored a book about the firm to be published later this year, he said.
Guinness said he also has a background as a journalist with Reuters and has been active in the parliament upper house.

Buying Amer is his first venture in sporting goods, and he said his return to playing an active part in business started with the acquisition of Swedish investment company Trustor announced two weeks ago.
Although close to each other in time, there was no "inherent connection" between the two acquisitions, he said.

He said he expected some unspecified marketing and advertising measures to accelerate Amer's turnaround, give positive publicity and boost its stock to make it possible to "grow cheaply". The effects could even come quickly, he said.
"It is extraordinary how quickly you can get results like that," he said, referring to experiences from his time with Guinness when it reversed declining profitability in the 1980s.
He said he expected to cooperate well with Amer CEO Roger Talermo, who in turn said it was positive that Guinness would set out to maintain the current strategy.
"But it is too early for me to make any judgement about how things will work out," Talermo told Reuters.
"I'm pretty sure we can work fairly well together," said Guinness.

Although the Wilson sporting brand was the key asset for Lord Moyne, he said there were no immediate plans to sell either of Amer's other parts -- the tobacco unit or the Time System unit which makes time planning systems.
